system_prompt_style.note: PromptsHandler formats prompt from customer profile/state.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Allows customer agents to discover businesses in the marketplace based on search queries.
env_context_strategy.note: Agent issues Search actions; lexical search is default.

context_compaction.note: Prompt rebuilt from full event history each step; no compaction code seen.

observation_format.note: Text messages plus structured proposal/payment dumps.

tool_call_format.note: Structured-output action object, not provider tool calls.

tool_count.evidence_quote: Our protocol consists of 5 unique actions: search, sending text messages, sending order proposals, sending payments, and fetching new messages.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Our protocol consists of 5 unique actions: search, sending text messages, sending order proposals, sending payments, and fetching new messages.
edit_primitive.note: No file editing in the action space.

tool_schema_source.note: Action schemas served from Pydantic action models via /protocol.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: `/actions/protocol` - Agents get the message protocol from the platform
protocol_standardization.note: Custom REST marketplace protocol; paper says it complements MCP/A2A but does not implement them.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
Our results, with baseline ReACT-style agents, indicate that when autonomous agents are equipped with capabilities for discovery, communication, and trans-
action execution
loop_primitives.note: Business agent reacts to fetched messages in a polling loop.

planning_granularity.note: One action chosen per step; no stored plan object.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Assistant Agents (representing consumers) and Service Agents (representing businesses) interact through a central Market Environment.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Sends a message from one agent to another. Supports three message types
delegation_mechanism.note: Central platform routes messages between agents.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: These results suggest benefits to human-in-the-loop designs where agents assist rather than replace human decision-making
human_in_loop.note: Stated as future work; agents run autonomously by default.

state_persistence.note: Results stored in DB; no resume path documented.

self_verification.note: Post-hoc welfare analytics, not in-run verification of agent output.

rollback.evidence_quote: Records all marketplace activity including agent registrations, actions executed, messages exchanged, and transactions completed.
rollback.note: Append-only action log; no revert mechanism.

if self._max_steps is not None and self.conversation_step >= self._max_steps:
            await self.logger.warning("Max steps exceeded, shutting down early!")
termination_condition.note: max_steps default 100; agent can call shutdown after ending transaction.

cost_controls.note: Per-response token cap; also max_concurrency for rate limiting.

timeouts.evidence_quote: polling_interval: Number of seconds to wait after fetching 0 messages.
timeouts.note: Only polling intervals and step caps found; no timeout enforcement in evidence.

Agents operate as independent clients while the marketplace environ-
ment serves as the central server, communicating through HTTP/REST endpoints.
execution_isolation.note: Agents run as local Python processes; Docker used only for the Postgres DB.

Within the action endpoint, we design specific message types that enable

filesystem_access.note: Agents act only on the simulated marketplace state in the DB; no filesystem tool.

network_policy.evidence_quote: Agents connect to the server via HTTP and interact through defined API endpoints.

permission_model.evidence_quote: The marketplace protocol defines the rules and available actions agents can perform.
permission_model.note: Only the five protocol actions are executable; API token required.

tracing.evidence_quote: **logs**: Captures agent decision-making processes and LLM interactions
